instructions: Chapter-wise questions from ICSE board, compartment and specimen papers, 2015–2024.

questions.question: A single-dimensional array contains N elements. What will be the last subscript?
questions.solution: (b) N-1. Subscripts start at 0, so N elements use subscripts 0 to N-1.

questions.topic: Accessing an index beyond the array
questions.question:
What is the value of temperature[5]? if the list of temperatures is defined as below
int[] temperature = {30, 40, 70, 10, 55};
questions.solution: (c) ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The array has 5 elements with indices 0 to 4, so index 5 does not exist and the access throws the exception at run time.

questions.topic: Length of a row of a 2D array
questions.question: In the declaration int x[][] = new int[3][50];, what does x[0].length return?
questions.solution: (b) 50. x.length is the number of rows (3); x[0] is the first row, which has 50 elements.

questions.question: Which of the following search techniques works on unsorted arrays?
questions.solution: (a) Linear Search. It checks elements one by one, so the order does not matter; binary search needs a sorted array, and the other two are not search techniques.

questions.topic: Binary search when value is smaller than middle
questions.question: In binary search, what happens when the value to be searched is less than the middle element?

options.a: The search continues in the second half of the array.
options.b: The search stops, as the value cannot be found.
options.c: The search continues in the first half of the array.

questions.solution: (c) The search continues in the first half of the array. In an ascending array a smaller value can only lie before the middle, so the upper bound becomes mid - 1.

questions.topic: Valid subscripts of an array of 10
questions.question: What is the range of valid subscripts for an array declared as int a[10];?
questions.solution: (c) 0 to 9. An array of 10 elements has subscripts from 0 to 10 - 1 = 9.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct representation of a two-dimensional array declaration?

options.a: data type array_variable = new data type[rows][columns];
options.c: data type array_variable[][] = new data type[rows][columns];
options.d: data type[][] array_variable = new data type[columns][rows];

questions.solution: (c) data type array_variable[][] = new data type[rows][columns];. The variable needs two pairs of brackets, and new allocates rows first, then columns.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the .length property in Java?

options.a: It can only be used with single-dimensional arrays.
options.b: It returns the total memory size of the array.
options.c: It returns the number of elements in a one-dimensional array or the size of a row in a two-dimensional array.
options.d: It always returns the size of the array minus one.

questions.solution: (c) It returns the number of elements in a one-dimensional array or the size of a row in a two-dimensional array. For a 2D array x, x[r].length gives the size of row r (and x.length gives the number of rows).

questions.question: Which sorting technique repeatedly swaps adjacent elements if they are in the wrong order?
questions.solution: (b) Bubble Sort. It compares neighbouring elements and swaps them when they are out of order, pass after pass.

questions.question: In selection sort, what happens during each iteration?

options.a: Adjacent elements are compared and swapped if necessary.
options.b: The largest element is moved to its correct position.
options.c: The smallest element is found and swapped with the current element.
options.d: All elements are divided into two halves and sorted recursively.

questions.solution: (c) The smallest element is found and swapped with the current element. Each pass selects the smallest remaining element and puts it in the next position (for ascending order).
(d) All of the above. Java does not allow a size inside the declaration brackets; an array of 5 ints is created with new int[5] (either bracket position) or by an initialiser list of 5 values.

questions.topic: Finding the length of an array
questions.solution: (a) Only A. The length of an array is the property nums.length (no brackets). nums[0].length would only compile if nums were a 2D array, and then it gives the length of the first row, not of nums; nums.length() is wrong because length is not a method for arrays. (Corrected: the source key said (d) Both A and B.)
(d) All of the above. Compared with the middle element, a smaller value lies in the first half, a larger value in the second half, and an equal value means it is found.
(b) (1) (2) (3) (4). Loop over the array, compare each element with the key, print "Found" on a match and then break out of the loop.

questions.topic: Order of statements to find array length
questions.question:
Consider the following program segment where statements are jumbled. Choose the correct order of statements to calculate the length of an array.
int arr[] = {10, 20, 30, 40}; // (1)
int length = arr.length;     // (2)
System.out.println(length);  // (3)
questions.solution: (a) (1) (2) (3). The array must exist before its length is read, and the length must be stored before it is printed.

questions.question: Write one difference between Linear Search and Binary Search.
questions.solution: Linear search checks the elements one by one from the start and works on sorted or unsorted arrays. Binary search works only on a sorted array: it compares the value with the middle element and keeps halving the search range, so it is much faster on long arrays.

marking_points.point: Linear search: element-by-element, works on unsorted arrays
Binary search: needs a sorted array, compares with middle element and halves the range
